boundaries.name: native-target-refinement
boundaries.obligation: Native `to_u64_vec` word lists and in-circuit `to_vec` target lists are represented by the same Lean lists. That the plonky2 builder emits exactly those wires, and that `builder.constant`/`range_check` behave as modelled, is not proved.

boundaries.name: field-and-range-discipline
boundaries.obligation: `Nat` stands for Goldilocks field elements, `u32` limbs and `u64` values. Canonicality and range checks appear as explicit hypotheses, never as type invariants; field arithmetic is not modelled.

boundaries.name: keccak-callback
boundaries.obligation: `solidity_keccak256` / `BuilderKeccak256::keccak256` is an opaque function. Nothing here assumes collision resistance, so the chain hash pins neither the contents nor the length of a chain except under that unproved assumption.

boundaries.name: plonky2-proof-soundness
boundaries.obligation: No proof object exists in this model. `verify_proof`, `conditionally_verify_cyclic_proof_or_dummy`, `add_verifier_data_public_inputs` and `cyclic_base_proof` are premises: the cyclic wrapper is modelled by its accept relation on public inputs, and a satisfied relation is NOT evidence that a proof exists or is sound.

boundaries.name: recursive-verifier-data-binding
boundaries.obligation: That the cyclic circuit's verifier data really pins the recursion to itself (`connect_hashes`/`connect_merkle_caps` in `add_proof_target_and_verify_cyclic`, and `common_data_for_hash_chain_circuit`'s gate padding) is assumed, not modelled.

boundaries.name: reward-attribution
boundaries.obligation: `proof_submitter` is an unconstrained circuit witness. Who is entitled to the aggregation reward must be enforced by the consumer of the chain-end proof; this model proves only that the statement accepts any address.
